days.title: Arrive in Interlaken
days.description: Trains do the work from the moment you land

activities.activity: Rail transfer from Zurich airport and check in between the two lakes
activities.notes: Swiss stations have lifts and level boarding — no stairs anywhere on this route

activities.activity: Level lakeside stroll along the Höheweg promenade
activities.notes: Flat, benches every couple of hundred metres, Jungfrau views to whet the appetite

activities.activity: Train to Lauterbrunnen and walk the paved valley-floor path to Staubbach Falls
activities.notes: About 2 km each way, entirely flat with a smooth surface — one of the great easy walks in the Alps, 72 waterfalls overhead

activities.activity: Coffee at a terrace café below the falls, bus back if legs are done
Cable car and mountain railway up to car-free Mürren
activities.notes: The lifts carry you to 1,650 m — the village lanes are gentle and compact

activities.activity: Funicular to Allmendhubel and the flower-trail loop
activities.notes: A 20-minute gravel loop, gently graded, face to face with Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau

activities.activity: Boat cruise across turquoise Lake Brienz to Giessbach
activities.notes: Step-free boarding at Interlaken Ost; lunch aboard

activities.activity: Historic funicular from the jetty to the Giessbach Falls terrace
activities.notes: The funicular removes all the climbing — the falls terrace is a 200 m level path

activities.activity: Gondola to First and the cliff-edge boardwalk
activities.notes: The First Cliff Walk is a railed, level boardwalk bolted to the cliff — genuinely thrilling, no steps

activities.activity: Walk the wide gravel trail towards Bachalpsee, turning at the halfway bench
activities.notes: Gently rolling; the 2 km out-and-back version keeps well inside your 5 km comfort zone

days.title: Schynige Platte heritage railway
days.description: 1893 cog railway to a natural balcony

activities.activity: Vintage cog train from Wilderswil up to Schynige Platte
activities.notes: 50 scenic minutes each way — the viewpoint is beside the station

activities.activity: Short walk through the alpine botanical garden and panorama lunch
activities.notes: Paths are graded and short, with the whole Jungfrau range laid out in front

days.title: Spiez and home
days.description: One last lake before the airport

activities.activity: Train along Lake Thun to Spiez castle gardens
activities.notes: Level gardens above the bay — an easy, beautiful full stop

activities.activity: Direct rail connection to Zurich airport for the flight home

finalText:
The Bernese Oberland in spring is made for exactly your brief: some of the most dramatic landscape in Europe, with a transport network — trains, boats, cable cars and funiculars — that does all the climbing so your legs never have to. This is a real mountain trip, not a compromise: you'll stand on a boardwalk bolted to a cliff at 2,168 m, ride an 1893 cog railway to a flower meadow, and walk beneath a 300 m waterfall, all on flat, well-surfaced, accessible paths.

Every walking day stays within your 5 km ceiling and each one has a shorter fallback: the valley-floor path at Lauterbrunnen is pancake-flat with benches, the Allmendhubel loop is 20 gentle minutes, and the Bachalpsee trail has a natural turnaround bench at halfway. Nothing here involves steps you can't avoid — Swiss stations and boats offer level or step-free boarding throughout, and May means fewer crowds on the lifts.

Estimated cost for two: £2,400 including flights, a half-board hotel in Interlaken all week (no hotel-hopping — one base, day trips out), and a regional travel pass covering the trains, boats and most lifts — just inside your £2,500 budget. Switzerland isn't cheap, but the pass makes the daily adventures feel free.

Want me to check spring opening dates for the First gondola and the Schynige Platte railway (both typically open from late May), or look at flight options?
